issues.description: The problem statement instructs that SealSaloon.orders should be a modifiable List<Meal>, but the provided solution (and the template utilities like ArrayHelpers) use an array (Meal[]). This mismatch between the specified collection type (List) and the array-based implementation will confuse students about which type to implement and which helpers to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and starter code consistent: either change the problem statement to request an array-based orders field (Meal[]) and explicitly reference ArrayHelpers, or update the template/solution to use a List<Meal> everywhere (and provide or remove array helper usage) so students have a single expected collection type.

issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradiction about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: earlier it instructs initializing the stock in the constructor as an (instance) final field, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). This inner contradiction will confuse students whether to implement stock as an instance final field initialized in the constructor or as a static field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: explicitly state that stock is a static (shared) attribute and remove or update the earlier wording that suggests initializing it as an instance final field in the constructor. Optionally note acceptable initialization locations (declaration or constructor) for the static final stock to avoid further confusion.
